title: Time Management Is Pain Management
coreMove: Treat a slipped schedule as evidence of avoided discomfort and plan the moment when that discomfort will be faced.
sourcePressure: The chapter turns the internal-trigger frame toward calendar behavior, showing that delay and respectable substitute tasks often protect the reader from discomfort.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would teach better scheduling without naming the pain that the schedule is being used to dodge.

hook: Time Management Is Pain Management as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: museum registrar delaying a loan-condition report
exampleSpecs.audience: registrar who keeps polishing labels instead of calling a lender about damage
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fragile textile shipment may be refused because the hard conversation keeps moving
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the exact awkward call into the 10:30 block instead of resizing gallery labels again
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A cotton glove rests on a textile crate inspection sheet.

exampleSpecs.domain: marathon aid-station coordinator avoiding volunteer assignments
exampleSpecs.audience: race volunteer lead who keeps editing the route map
exampleSpecs.stakes: unassigned mile posts will leave runners without water
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he marks 'fear of disappointing friends' on the volunteer grid and sends the first hard assignment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A laminated route map curls beside a volunteer grid.

exampleSpecs.domain: tax preparer postponing a messy self-employed return
exampleSpecs.audience: preparer using tidy W-2 files to avoid one ambiguous client
exampleSpecs.stakes: the client misses a filing window because uncertainty got renamed efficiency
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she blocks forty minutes for the unclear mileage folder and closes the easy return stack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A mileage folder with fuel receipts sits apart from neat W-2 packets.

exampleSpecs.domain: marine conservation diver delaying equipment inventory
exampleSpecs.audience: field lead who checks grant email to avoid finding broken gear
exampleSpecs.stakes: tomorrow's reef survey depends on tanks and sensors being ready
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, he refreshes the inbox; after, he writes 'bad news risk' beside the oxygen checklist and starts counting tanks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A slate oxygen checklist hangs from a dive crate.

exampleSpecs.domain: film colorist avoiding notes from a demanding director
exampleSpecs.audience: freelancer who tweaks easy scenes rather than opening the hard note set
exampleSpecs.stakes: delivery day gets squeezed by polite avoidance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she drags the director notes into the first block and names the dread before touching the color wheels
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A control surface glows beside a red folder of director notes.

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital pharmacy technician delaying a controlled-substance count
exampleSpecs.audience: technician doing restocking to avoid the tense double-count
exampleSpecs.stakes: shift handoff becomes unsafe when anxiety is hidden under busyness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she tells the lead, 'I am avoiding the count because I hate being watched,' then opens the vault log
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A vault log sits beside a tamper seal packet.
